processing: An unoxidised green tea made in two recognised shapes, tightly curled and flat pressed. The steps themselves are not spelled out in the description of the protected product.
harvest_season: Not specifically recorded; spring is the usual prized picking for greens of this kind.
appearance_dry: Either tight, fine, glossy green curls, or smooth, flat, even leaves with visible down.
appearance_liquor: Bright yellow-green for the curled style, clear golden-yellow for the flat style.
taste_profile: The curled style is rich, fresh and strongly aromatic; the flat style is fresh and mellow with some sweetness and a clean, plain aroma.

brewing.notes: General guidance for a Guizhou green. Go a little cooler, around 80°C, with the flat style.

vintage_note: A regional appellation with no single season on record. As is usual for greens, buy the current year's spring tea and drink it within the year, and check which of the two shapes you are getting.
description:
Qinglong Green Tea is a county appellation from the deeply cut karst mountains of Qinglong in southwest Guizhou, where the land runs from 543 metres up to 2025 metres. Rather than one fixed tea, the name covers two styles: curled and flat.

The two taste different. The curled style is the stronger one, with a lasting aroma, a bright yellow-green cup and a rich, fresh flavour. The flat style has visible down, a clear golden cup and a fresh, mellow, sweet and full flavour.

Brew it like other Guizhou greens, with water around 85°C for the curled tea and slightly cooler for the flat, and short enough steeps to keep it fresh.

The protected area covers 14 townships and subdistricts of the county. Since this is a name for a place more than a single recipe, the shape and harvest date on the packet are what tell you what you are buying.
history: Little is documented about the early history of tea in Qinglong under this name. It is the modern record that stands out: geographical indication protection was approved in December 2017, and the county has worked on mechanising and standardising production, with the tea now named among Guizhou's notable teas.
